artworks.title: Daedalus and Pasiphaë
artworks.description: Lemaire stages the carpenter's gift: Daedalus presents the hollow wooden cow to the Cretan queen whose desire for Poseidon's bull will beget the Minotaur. Oil on canvas, Musée des Beaux-Arts d'Agen (Louvre deposit).

artworks.title: Pasiphaë
artworks.description: Moreau's Symbolist Pasiphaë turns the queen's unnatural passion into jewelled nightmare — Helios' daughter and the bull myth as fin-de-siècle obsession rather than classical anecdote. Musée Gustave Moreau, Paris.

artworks.title: Daedalus Presenting the Wooden Cow to Pasiphaë
artworks.description: From the House of the Vettii at Pompeii, the fresco shows Daedalus unveiling the wooden cow to Queen Pasiphaë — the craft that lets her mate with the bull and stain Minos' house. Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (inv. 8979).

artworks.title: Pasiphaë Adorning the Bull with Flowers
artworks.description: Cros's pâte-de-verre relief freezes the queen in the act of garlanding the bull — Pasiphaë's doomed courtship cast in coloured glass for the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

artworks.title: Pasiphaë and the Minotaur
artworks.description: On the tondo of an Attic red-figure kylix from Vulci, Pasiphaë faces the child she bore — the Minotaur already horned beside his mother. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Cabinet des Médailles (De Ridder 1066).

popCulture.title: The King Must Die
popCulture.creator: Mary Renault
popCulture.description: Renault's Theseus novel rebuilds Minoan Crete around the bull-court: Pasiphaë's world of sacred kings and the labyrinth that waits for the tribute.

popCulture.title: The Bull from the Sea
popCulture.creator: Mary Renault
popCulture.description: Renault's sequel keeps Pasiphaë's Crete in view as Theseus' world widens — the bull-kingdom and the queen whose passion shaped the labyrinth's shadow.

popCulture.title: Pasiphaë
popCulture.description: Pasiphaë endures as the witch-queen of the bull — Helios' daughter whose unnatural desire begot the Minotaur and stained the house of Minos.
